subject: Civil Engineering
title: Shear Force: The Sliding Danger
description: A quick win: understand Shear Force: The Sliding Danger.

hook.text: Scissors cut paper by pushing two blades past each other. That's shear force.

buildup.text: In structures, shear happens when forces push opposite sides in different directions.

discovery.text: Beams near their supports face the highest shear — the load tries to slide them apart.

twist.text: Shear failure is sudden with no warning — the material just snaps in two.

climax.text: Engineers add stirrups inside concrete beams to catch shear before it starts.

punchline.text: Shear is invisible until it's catastrophic.

quiz.question: Where do beams experience the highest shear force?
options: At the center of the span
Near the supports at each end
At the top surface of the beam

details.summary: Shear force is the internal sliding force acting perpendicular to a beam's length at any cross-section. It tends to make one part of the beam slide vertically past the adjacent part. Shear force is maximum at beam supports and zero at midspan under uniform loading.
details.whyItMatters: Shear failure gives little warning and can cause catastrophic collapse. Adequate shear reinforcement, particularly in concrete beams with stirrups, is essential because concrete is very weak in the diagonal tension that shear produces.
takeaways: Shear force is highest near supports and lowest at midspan for uniformly loaded beams
Shear produces diagonal tension cracks in concrete beams at roughly 45 degrees
Steel stirrups cross potential diagonal cracks to provide shear reinforcement

faq.question: Why is shear failure in concrete considered more dangerous than bending failure?
faq.answer: Bending failure in properly reinforced concrete is gradual, with visible cracking and large deflection providing warning before collapse. Shear failure is sudden and explosive because diagonal cracks propagate rapidly through concrete weakened by diagonal tension.

faq.question: How do stirrups prevent shear failure in reinforced concrete beams?
faq.answer: Stirrups are vertical or inclined steel loops that cross the path of potential diagonal shear cracks. When a diagonal crack forms, the stirrups that cross it resist opening by developing tensile force. They also confine the concrete and enable aggregate interlock across the crack.
